clarification.retaining_write_restricted: Removing broad restricting SIDs while retaining WRITE_RESTRICTED does not, by itself, introduce a new generic read-capability requirement. The read-capability closure discussed for a token without WRITE_RESTRICTED is a different design.
static_required_changes: The current dedicated-account token helper adds User and the Include branch adds Logon plus Everyone. Removing only Everyone leaves broad identity alternatives; the existing helper cannot produce the proposed capability-only set unchanged.
desktop.rs explicitly refuses private=false when a nonempty restricting list lacks the token Logon SID. This refusal must remain.
clarification.independent_parent_delete_boundary: legacy_admission.rs records an earlier native FILE_DELETE_CHILD counterexample for WRITE_RESTRICTED. Removing broad restricting SIDs does not by itself establish that the separate parent-directory delete route is blocked.
native_unproven: Exact child TokenRestrictedSids, TokenGroups and TokenPrivileges for the original elevated execution were not observed.

Capability-only launch through WinSta0 and the owned private desktop, shared route-SID interactions, WFP identity compatibility and newly created object ACLs require actual qualification; this review does not claim each is a proven unconditional startup failure.

All four original outside-delete cells must still be checked under the actual child token. The parent Backup/Restore observations in the later Bazel ordinary-host failure are a separate observation and do not identify the dedicated elevated child token.

primary_docs.observed: WRITE_RESTRICTED applies restricting SIDs only when evaluating write access; the page does not separately prove the FILE_DELETE_CHILD parent fallback behavior.
The general restricting-SID access-check model does not replace the exact native four-cell qualification.
